$description: Read by Storybook and AI tools. One entry per component.

components.name: Button
components.description: People press buttons to do something, like save or pay.

props.name: variant
props.notes: Pick one primary button per screen.

props.name: size
props.notes: Height comes from the screen type and text size.

props.name: fullWidth
props.notes: Use on phones for the main action.

props.name: loading
props.notes: Shows a spinner and blocks double taps.

props.name: disabled
props.notes: Avoid it. Explain what is missing instead.

components.accessibility: Uses a real button element. The keyboard focus outline is always visible. Words must be at least 4.5 to 1 against the button.
components.guidance: Use one main (primary) button for the most important action on a screen. Use the outline button for Cancel or Back. Write the label as a short action that says what will happen, like "Save my changes." Keep the label on one line. Do not use a button to go to another website. Use a link instead.

components.name: Icon button
components.description: A small button that shows only a picture, like a trash can or a close X.

props.name: label
props.notes: Required. Read out loud by screen readers.

props.name: showLabel
props.notes: Shows the label under the icon.

components.accessibility: Every icon button has a hidden label for screen readers. The tap area is the full control height, even when the icon is small.
components.guidance: Only use an icon button when the picture is very common, like X for close or a trash can for delete. Always give it a label. When there is room, show the label as a word too.

components.name: Button group
components.description: A few buttons joined together. People pick one, like Day, Week, or Month.
components.accessibility: Works like a set of radio buttons. Arrow keys move between choices. The chosen button says 'selected' to screen readers.
components.guidance: Use a button group to switch between views of the same thing. Keep it to five choices or fewer. For choices in a form, use radio buttons instead.

components.name: Link
components.description: Words people click to go to another page. Includes action links and back links.

props.name: variant
props.notes: 'action' starts a main task. 'back' goes one step back.

props.name: external
props.notes: Adds an icon and says 'opens a new tab'.

components.accessibility: Link words must make sense alone, like 'View your claims', not 'Click here'. External links say they open a new tab.
components.guidance: Use a link to go somewhere. Use a button to do something. Use an action link, not a button, to start a main task from a page, like 'Find a doctor'. Never write 'click here'.

components.name: Text field
components.description: A box where people type, with a label and help text.

props.name: label
props.notes: Required. Always shown above the box.

props.name: autocomplete
props.notes: Lets the browser fill it in.

props.name: width
props.notes: Match the width to the answer.

components.accessibility: The label is connected to the box. Help and error text are read out with it. Errors are never shown by color alone.
components.guidance: Every field needs a label above it. Put help text under the field, not inside it as gray placeholder text. When something is wrong, say what is wrong and how to fix it, in one sentence.

components.name: Text area
components.description: A big box for longer answers, like a note to a doctor. It can count characters.
components.accessibility: The character count updates for screen readers after the person stops typing, not on every key.
components.guidance: Use a text area when the answer may be more than one line. Tell people how much to write. If there is a limit, show the count so they are not surprised.

components.name: Select
components.description: A list people open to pick one choice.

props.name: placeholder
props.notes: Only 'Choose one'. Never a real choice.

components.accessibility: On phones and tablets, it is the browser's own select, so it works with every screen reader and opens the phone's own picker. With a mouse, it is a button that opens a list. Focus stays on the button. Arrow keys, Home, End, and typing a letter move through the choices. Enter or Space picks one. Esc closes the list and keeps the old choice.
components.guidance: Use a dropdown when there are 5 to 15 choices. For 2 to 4 choices, show them all as radio buttons instead. Sort choices in an order people expect, like by date or A to Z.

components.name: Checkbox
components.description: A small box people tick. They can pick more than one.

props.name: label
props.notes: Required. Clicking it ticks the box.

props.name: checked
props.notes: 'mixed' is for a parent box with some children ticked.

components.accessibility: The whole label is part of the tap area. Groups sit inside a fieldset with a legend that asks the question.
components.guidance: Use checkboxes when people can pick more than one choice, or to agree to something. Put each choice on its own line. Never start with a box already ticked for anything that costs money or shares data.

components.name: Radio buttons
components.description: A list of round buttons. People pick only one choice.

props.name: layout
props.notes: Only use inline for Yes and No.

components.accessibility: Arrow keys move between choices. The group has a legend. Nothing is chosen at the start unless there is a safe default.
components.guidance: Use radio buttons when people must pick exactly one of 2 to 6 choices. Show every choice, do not hide them in a dropdown. For Yes and No questions, put Yes first.

components.name: Switch
components.description: An on and off control that works right away, like turning on text reminders.

props.name: onChange
props.notes: Saves right away. No Save button.

components.accessibility: Uses role switch, so screen readers say 'on' or 'off'.
components.guidance: Use a switch only for settings that take effect right away. Inside a form that has a Submit button, use a checkbox instead.

components.name: Combobox (search and pick)
components.description: A box that shows matches as people type, like finding a medicine or a doctor.

props.name: allowFreeText
props.notes: Can people keep words that are not in the list?

components.accessibility: Follows the ARIA combobox pattern. Focus stays in the box. Up and down arrows move through matches, and Home and End jump to the first and last one. Enter picks a match. Esc closes the list. The number of matches is read out.
components.guidance: Use a combobox when there are too many choices for a dropdown, like medicines, doctors, or cities. Forgive spelling mistakes. Show 'No matches' with a next step when nothing is found.

components.name: Search field
components.description: A box to search the site or a list.
components.accessibility: Sits inside a search landmark. The button has a label even when it shows only an icon.
components.guidance: Put site search in the header. Show what people searched for and how many results there are. Keep their words in the box after they search.

components.name: Date input (known date)
components.description: Three small boxes for month, day, and year. Use it for dates people know, like a birth date.
components.accessibility: Three plain number boxes in a fieldset. Uses the number keyboard on phones. Each box has its own label. Errors say which box is wrong.
components.guidance: Use this for dates people already know, like a birth date or the date a card was issued. Never make people scroll back years in a calendar. Use the date picker only for dates they need to choose, like an appointment.

components.name: Date picker
components.description: A date box with a small calendar that pops open. Use it for picking a new date, like an appointment.

props.name: typeable
props.notes: People can always type the date instead.

components.accessibility: People can always type the date. The calendar is a grid: arrow keys move by day, Page Up and Page Down move by month. Turned-off days say why.
components.guidance: Use a date picker for picking a new date within a few months, like a visit or a delivery. Always let people type the date too. Turn off days that cannot be picked and say why. For birth dates, use the date input.

components.name: Time picker
components.description: A list of times to pick from, like 10:30 AM.
components.accessibility: Works as a combobox. People can type '1030' or '10:30a' and it understands.
components.guidance: Use 12-hour time with AM and PM. Only show times that can be picked. For appointments, show open times as buttons with the appointment slot picker instead.

components.name: Formatted fields
components.description: Boxes that help people type things in the right shape, like a phone number, ZIP code, or member ID.
components.accessibility: Formatting is added as people type, but they can also paste any format. Screen readers hear the format in the hint.
components.guidance: Accept numbers typed any way, with or without dashes or spaces, and fix the format for people. Never ask for a full Social Security number when the last 4 digits will do.

components.name: Number and money
components.description: Boxes for amounts, like how many refills or how much to pay.
components.accessibility: Uses the number keyboard. Plus and minus buttons have labels, like 'Add one'.
components.guidance: Show the dollar sign outside the box so people do not have to type it. Use plus and minus buttons for small counts. Say the limits in the help text.

components.name: File upload
components.description: A place to add files, like a photo of a bill or a letter from a doctor.
components.accessibility: There is always a real 'Choose a file' button. Dragging is extra, never the only way. Progress and errors are read out.
components.guidance: Say which file types and sizes are OK before people pick a file. On phones, let people take a photo. Show each file with a way to remove it.

components.name: Label and help text
components.description: The words above a field that say what to type, and the smaller words that help.

props.name: for
props.notes: Connects the label to its field.

components.accessibility: Labels are always visible, never only inside the box. A red star alone is not enough, so the word is written out.
components.guidance: Write labels as short, plain questions or nouns. Put help text under the label, before the box. Mark the optional fields with the word '(optional)'.

components.name: Error message
components.description: Red words under a field that say what is wrong and how to fix it.

props.name: message
props.notes: Say what is wrong and how to fix it.

components.accessibility: Never uses color alone. The icon and the words carry the meaning. The field is marked invalid for screen readers.
components.guidance: Write one short sentence that says how to fix the problem, like 'Enter a ZIP code with 5 numbers.' Do not blame the person. Do not say 'invalid'.

components.name: Fieldset (question group)
components.description: A group of fields that answer one question, like an address.

props.name: legend
props.notes: Required. The question for the group.

components.accessibility: Uses a real fieldset and legend so screen readers read the question before each field.
components.guidance: Group fields that belong to one question, like the parts of an address or a date. Write the legend as the question.

components.name: Error summary
components.description: A box at the top of a form that lists every problem, with links to each one.
components.accessibility: Gets keyboard focus when the form is sent with problems, so screen readers read it first. Each link jumps to the field.
components.guidance: Show the error summary at the top when someone sends a form with problems. Use the same words as the error under each field. Move focus to it.

components.name: Alert
components.description: A message inside the page that tells people something important.
components.accessibility: Every tone has its own icon and a hidden word like 'Warning:'. New alerts are announced with a live region.
components.guidance: Use alerts for things people need to know on this page. Start with the most important words. Say what to do next. Do not stack more than two.

components.name: Notification banner
components.description: A strip across the top of the page for news that affects everyone.
components.accessibility: Sits in its own region at the top. The close button has a label. Closing it moves focus back to the page.
components.guidance: Use one banner at a time, for news that matters to everyone, like a service outage or open enrollment. Keep it to one sentence and one link.

components.name: Toast
components.description: A short message that pops up after an action, like 'Saved'. It can offer Undo.
components.accessibility: Announced politely. It stays while the mouse or keyboard focus is on it. Never the only place important news appears.
components.guidance: Use a toast to confirm something worked. Keep it to a few words. Never put an error or anything people must read in a toast.

components.name: Progress bar
components.description: A bar that fills up to show how much is done.
components.accessibility: Uses role progressbar with the value. The words above it say the same thing as the bar.
components.guidance: Always show words with the bar, like 'Step 2 of 4' or '60% uploaded'. For steps with names, use the step list.

components.name: Spinner
components.description: A turning circle that says 'please wait'.
components.accessibility: Has a label read by screen readers. It stops turning for people who turn off motion.
components.guidance: Show a spinner only if waiting takes more than 1 second. Say what is loading. If it takes more than 10 seconds, show a progress bar instead.

components.name: Loading placeholder (skeleton)
components.description: Gray shapes that show where things will appear while the page loads.
components.accessibility: Hidden from screen readers. The page says 'Loading' in words instead. The pulse stops for people who turn off motion.
components.guidance: Use loading shapes when you know the layout of what is coming, like a list of claims. Match the shapes to the real content.

components.name: Empty state
components.description: What a page shows when there is nothing there yet, with a next step.
components.accessibility: The title is a heading. The picture is hidden from screen readers.
components.guidance: Say why the page is empty and what people can do next. Give one main action. Do not use jokes.

components.name: Session timeout warning
components.description: A message that warns people before they are signed out, so they do not lose their work.
components.accessibility: Moves focus to the message and announces it. One key press keeps people signed in. Required by WCAG 2.2.1 when time runs out.
components.guidance: Warn people before a timeout and let them stay signed in with one click. Save what they typed so nothing is lost if they are signed out.

components.name: Card
components.description: A box that groups things that belong together.

props.name: href
props.notes: Makes the whole card a link.

components.accessibility: If the whole card is a link, only the title is the link text. The rest is read as a description.
components.guidance: Use a card to group things that belong together, like one account or one order. Do not put a card inside another card. Keep one main action per card.

components.name: Badge and tag
components.description: A small label that shows a status, like 'In network' or 'Due soon'.

props.name: tone
props.values: neutral | brand | info | success | warning | danger

props.name: icon
props.notes: Status tones always have an icon.

components.accessibility: Color is never the only signal. Status badges have an icon and clear words.
components.guidance: Use badges for short statuses. One to three words. Use the same words for the same status everywhere, like 'Due soon' and never 'Due shortly'.

components.name: Avatar
components.description: A small picture or initials that stand for a person, like your doctor.

props.name: name
props.notes: Required. Used for initials and the label.

components.accessibility: Shows the person's name as text nearby. The picture has empty alt text when the name is already shown.
components.guidance: Show a photo when you have one. Otherwise show initials. Always show the name next to it.

components.name: Accordion
components.description: A list of headings that open to show more, like questions and answers.

props.name: multiple
props.notes: Can more than one be open?

components.accessibility: Each heading is a button inside a heading tag. It says 'expanded' or 'collapsed'.
components.guidance: Use an accordion to hide details most people do not need, like frequently asked questions. Never hide the most important information in one.

components.name: Summary list
components.description: Rows of labels and answers, with a Change link. Use it on review pages.
components.accessibility: Uses a description list. The Change links have hidden words, like 'Change phone number'.
components.guidance: Use a summary list to show answers before people submit. Give each row its own Change link that goes back to that question.

components.name: Inset text and warning
components.description: Text set apart from the page, for a key point or a safety warning.
components.accessibility: Warnings start with the hidden word 'Important:'. They never rely on color alone.
components.guidance: Use inset text for one key point. Use the warning callout for safety information, like when to call 911.

components.name: Divider
components.description: A thin line that separates parts of a page.
components.accessibility: Decorative lines are hidden from screen readers.
components.guidance: Use space before you use a line. Add a divider only when two parts of a page could be confused.

components.name: Tooltip
components.description: A small note that appears when people point at or focus on something.
components.accessibility: Shows on keyboard focus too, not only mouse over. Esc closes it. It stays while the mouse is over it (WCAG 1.4.13).
components.guidance: Use tooltips only for short names of icons. Never put important information in a tooltip, because people on phones cannot see it. Use the help drawer for explanations.

components.name: Popover
components.description: A small box that opens next to a button, with a bit more information or a few actions.
components.accessibility: Opens on click, not mouse over. Focus moves into it. Esc closes it and returns focus to the button.
components.guidance: Use a popover for a short explanation or a few actions tied to one button. For longer help, use the help drawer.

components.name: Icon
components.description: Small pictures that help people scan, like a phone or a calendar.

props.name: label
props.notes: Only when the icon stands alone.

components.accessibility: Icons next to words are hidden from screen readers. Icons that stand alone have a label.
components.guidance: Use icons next to words, not instead of them. Use the same icon for the same idea everywhere.

components.name: Header
components.description: The strip at the top of every page, with the logo, main links, and account.
components.accessibility: Starts with a skip link. The main links sit in a nav landmark. On phones, the menu button says 'Menu' in words.
components.guidance: Use the same header on every page. Keep five main links or fewer. On consumer screens, show the phone number.

components.name: Footer
components.description: The bottom of every page, with help, legal links, and the phone number.
components.accessibility: Sits in a footer landmark. Link groups have headings.
components.guidance: Put help, contact, privacy, and nondiscrimination notices in the footer. Show the phone number and hours.

components.name: Side navigation
components.description: A list of links down the side of the page, for moving around a section.
components.accessibility: The current page is marked with aria-current and is not shown by color alone.
components.guidance: Use side navigation for sections with more than five pages, mostly on employee screens. Keep two levels at most.

components.name: Tabs
components.description: A row of labels that switch between views on the same page.
components.accessibility: Follows the ARIA tabs pattern. Arrow keys move between tabs. The chosen tab has a thick line, not only a color.
components.guidance: Use tabs to switch between related views, like Medical and Pharmacy claims. Do not use tabs for steps in a process.

components.name: Breadcrumbs
components.description: A trail of links that shows where you are, like Home, then My plan, then Claims.
components.accessibility: Sits in a nav landmark named 'Breadcrumb'. The last item is the current page and is not a link.
components.guidance: Use breadcrumbs on pages that are three or more levels deep. On phones, show only the link one level up.

components.name: Pagination
components.description: Links to move between pages of a long list.
components.accessibility: Sits in a nav landmark. The current page is marked with aria-current. Previous and Next say it in words.
components.guidance: Say how many items there are, like 'Showing 1 to 20 of 240'. Always spell out Previous and Next.

components.name: Step list
components.description: Shows the steps of a task, which ones are done, and which one is next.
components.accessibility: Each step says its status in words, like 'done' or 'current step'. Done steps can be links back.
components.guidance: Use a step list for tasks with 3 to 6 named steps, like signing up. Let people go back to finished steps. Save their answers as they go.

components.name: Skip link
components.description: A hidden link that appears when people use the Tab key. It jumps past the header.
components.accessibility: Required for keyboard users (WCAG 2.4.1). It is the first thing on every page.
components.guidance: Put a skip link at the very top of every page. It shows only when it has keyboard focus.

components.name: Menu
components.description: A list of actions that opens from a button, like Edit, Print, or Delete.
components.accessibility: Follows the ARIA menu button pattern. Arrow keys move through items. Esc closes it.
components.guidance: Use a menu for extra actions. Put the most used action first and anything that deletes last, in red, after a line.

components.name: Pop-up (dialog)
components.description: A small window that asks a question before going on.
components.accessibility: Focus moves into the dialog and stays there. Esc closes it. Focus returns to the button that opened it.
components.guidance: Only use a pop-up when the person must decide something before going on, like confirming a delete. The title asks the question. The main button repeats the action, like "Delete this address," not "OK."

components.name: Drawer
components.description: A panel that slides in from the side, for a form or details without leaving the page.
components.accessibility: Works like a dialog. Focus moves in and stays in. Esc closes it. On phones it fills the screen.
components.guidance: Use a drawer for a short task or details about one item, like editing one claim. Use a full page for anything long.

components.name: Help drawer
components.description: A panel that explains a hard word or rule in plain words, without leaving the page.
components.accessibility: The help link says what it opens, like 'What is a deductible? Opens help.'
components.guidance: Use a help drawer for insurance words people may not know, like deductible or prior authorization. Explain them in one or two short paragraphs, with an example.

components.name: Data table
components.description: A table for lots of rows, with sorting, filters, row picking, and pages. Most used on employee screens.
components.accessibility: Uses a real table with column headers. Sort buttons say the sort order. Picking rows tells screen readers how many are picked. Scrolls sideways on phones without breaking the page.
components.guidance: Use a data table to compare many rows. Right-align numbers and money. Let people sort and filter. On phones, show a list of cards instead when there are more than 4 columns.

components.name: List
components.description: A simple list of items, like recent claims, each with a link to more.
components.accessibility: Uses a real list. Each row has one link, on the title, so screen readers do not hear it twice.
components.guidance: Use a list for a few items people scan, like recent claims. On phones, use a list instead of a wide table.

components.name: Filter chips
components.description: Small buttons that turn filters on and off, like 'In network' or 'Accepting new patients'.
components.accessibility: Each chip is a toggle button that says 'pressed' when on. A check mark shows it is on, not only color.
components.guidance: Use filter chips for 2 to 8 common filters above a list. Show how many results match. Always offer 'Clear all'.

components.name: Chart
components.description: Simple bar and line charts, like costs by month.

props.name: tableView
props.notes: Every chart has a table view.

components.accessibility: Every chart has a title, a short summary in words, and a table view. Hovering or focusing a bar shows its value. One series uses one color, so color never carries meaning alone.
components.guidance: Say the main point in the chart title, like 'Your costs went down in August.' Use one color for one series. Always offer a table view. Never use two y-axes.

components.name: Stack
components.description: Puts things in a column or row with even space between them.
components.accessibility: Only changes layout. It never changes the reading order.
components.guidance: Use Stack for all spacing between things. Never add margins by hand. Pick the gap from the spacing tokens.

components.name: Grid
components.description: Lines up content in columns that change with the screen size.
components.accessibility: Only changes layout. The reading order stays the same as the code order.
components.guidance: Use the grid for page layouts. Use 4 columns on phones and 12 on computers. Cards should span whole columns.

components.name: Container
components.description: Keeps a page from getting too wide, so lines of text are easy to read.
components.accessibility: Keeps lines near 65 characters, which is easier to read. Text can still grow to 200% without scrolling sideways.
components.guidance: Put text-heavy pages in the reading container. Put dashboards and tables in the page container.

components.name: Member ID card
components.description: A digital copy of the member's insurance card.
components.accessibility: All card details are real text, not a picture, so they can be read out and made bigger.
components.guidance: Show the member card as text people can read and zoom, with Print and Download. Put the member ID in large type. Show the phone numbers from the back of the card.

components.name: Provider card
components.description: A doctor or clinic in search results, with the key facts to choose one.

props.name: provider
props.values: {name, specialty, distance, network, accepting, languages, phone}

components.accessibility: The name is a heading and the only link. Status badges have words and icons.
components.guidance: Show whether the doctor is in network and accepting new patients first. Show the distance and phone number. Give one main action.

components.name: Medication item
components.description: One medicine, with how to take it, refills, and a Refill button.
components.accessibility: Drug names are real text so they can be read out. Instructions use plain words, not codes like 'BID'.
components.guidance: Write instructions in plain words, like 'Take 1 tablet by mouth 2 times a day.' Never use short codes. Show refills left and when the medicine runs out.

components.name: Lab result
components.description: A test result with the normal range, so people can see if it is high or low.
components.accessibility: High and low are written in words with an icon. The bar has a text version: 'Your result, 6.8, is above the normal range of 4.0 to 5.6.'
components.guidance: Say in words if a result is normal, high, or low. Show the normal range. Link to a plain explanation. Suggest talking to the doctor for anything flagged.

components.name: Appointment slot picker
components.description: Open visit times shown as big buttons, grouped by day and time of day.
components.accessibility: Each time is a button with the full date and time as its label. The chosen time is marked with a check, not only color.
components.guidance: Show open times as big buttons, grouped by Morning and Afternoon. Show the next few days first. Always show the time zone and the visit length.

components.name: Plan comparison
components.description: Two or three plans side by side, so people can compare costs and benefits.
components.accessibility: Built as a table on computers and as stacked cards on phones. Each row label is a row header.
components.guidance: Compare no more than 3 plans at once. Put the monthly cost and yearly limit first. Use the same row order for every plan. Mark the person's current plan.

components.name: Cost estimate
components.description: Shows what a service costs, what the plan pays, and what the member pays.
components.accessibility: The split bar has the same numbers written out in words next to it.
components.guidance: Put what the member pays in the biggest type. Show what the plan pays too. Say it is an estimate and what it is based on.

components.name: Consent and signature
components.description: A way to read terms, agree, and sign with a typed name.

props.name: onSign
props.notes: Saves the time and the words agreed to.

components.accessibility: The terms can be read at any zoom and downloaded. The typed name field says what it means: 'Typing your name counts as your signature.'
components.guidance: Summarize the terms in plain words at the top. Let people download the full text. Say that typing their name is their signature. Show the date.

icons.$description: The only icons teams should use. Names match lucide-react (Calendar for calendar, HeartPulse for heart-pulse). Always put words next to an icon, or give a lone icon a label.
